chapter: Georgie Auld, Hawkins and Los Angeles
title: The Crimson Canary film and the Red Nichols Capitol date
summary: McGhee recalls the film and how Dave Dexter brought Red Nichols to replace him on the Capitol session, which failed.

bands.name: Red Nichols and His Five Pennies

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: But what about that movie you made, The Crimson Canary?
What do you remember about that?

Well, I remember the (?) in Hollywood, "Hollywood Stampede" I think they called it -- [SINGS 4 BARS]; I remember that. And I remember... It was nice. I thought it came out very nice. I saw the picture a couple of times, too, since they made it.

But right after that is when we went into the studio at Capitol Records. Dave Dexter brought in Red Nichols to play in my place, you know. When they started rehearsing it down, he didn't have the slightest idea what he was supposed to be playing. So he really couldn't play it. So Oscar

would look at me and laugh, you know. So finally, they decided that he couldn't make the date. So he comes over to me, he says, "Oh, man, I really feel bad, but boy, that's a hard tune to play." I said, "Well, I don't feel bad, because I can play it," you know. I didn't stop to think or whatever... You know, I shouldn't have said that to him. You know, I didn't have too much finesse at that time. So I said, "Well, I ain't worried about it, because I can play it. I've been playing it every night, so I know I can play it."
So anyway, Dave Dexter really hated me then! "I don't like this guy, because every time I go to pull a piece on him, he pulls out the trump card."
Well, it was really unfair of Dave Dexter to try to put Red Nichols in that situation.

Yeah, you dig? Because Dave didn't have the slightest idea what was happening with the music. He didn't know. He thought, "Well, this is a famous guy. He can go off and play all that kind of music." But even the famous guys couldn't play that kind of music. I mean, a lot of guys didn't know what that kind of music was! And it was a very different situation for Red Nichols to come out of his Pennies and come and play with Coleman Hawkins. Which Hawk was a stepping stone himself, you know! I mean, he wasn't
no slouch when he made "Body and Soul", you know. So that's what I have say.
